title: Salesloft vs Zoho CRM: Engagement Workflows vs CRM System of Record
description: A practical decision guide to Salesloft and Zoho CRM. Salesloft is used for coordinate sales engagement, follow-ups, and rep activity; Zoho CRM is used for manage customer records, leads, accounts, and opportunities. Compare the actual workflow, data ownership, integrations, implementation effort, and total cost. Current pricing and plan limits are not independently verified here, so check official vendor terms before purchasing.

verdict: Salesloft and Zoho CRM are not automatic substitutes: sales engagement helps coordinate outreach, while CRM records organize customer and pipeline information. A team may need both, so document data ownership and handoffs before deciding. Run a small pilot with written success criteria. Verify current capabilities, plan limits, security and privacy terms, integrations, data export, and renewal conditions directly with each vendor. PilotStack has not recorded a controlled, current benchmark establishing a universal winner for this pair.

faqs.question: What is the main difference between Salesloft and Zoho CRM?
faqs.answer: Salesloft focuses on coordinate sales engagement, follow-ups, and rep activity; Zoho CRM focuses on manage customer records, leads, accounts, and opportunities. Compare them against the job your team needs to complete instead of treating ratings or feature counts as proof of a universal winner.

faqs.question: Can Salesloft replace Zoho CRM?
faqs.answer: Do not assume so. List the specific workflows, records, controls, reports, and integrations you depend on in Zoho CRM; test whether Salesloft meets each requirement before changing systems.

faqs.question: Can a team use Salesloft and Zoho CRM together?
faqs.answer: Potentially, if the team needs both workflows. Define which product owns each data field and process step, how records synchronize, how duplicates are handled, and who maintains the integration.

faqs.question: How should I compare their pricing?
faqs.answer: Use current vendor quotes for the same team size and workload. Include seats, usage limits, add-ons, implementation, integration work, training, administration, support, and renewal terms.

faqs.question: What should I test before choosing?
faqs.answer: Use realistic sample data and the same written acceptance criteria for both products. Record workflow completion, missing capabilities, reporting quality, migration effort, permissions, export options, and the total cost to operate.
